newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close higher on futures, CRT shr sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close higher on futures, CRT shr sale.

text.p: Brazil stocks ended strongly higher as the sale of a minority stake Rio Grande do Sul state's telecom sent phone company shares surging and as investors speculated ahead of Wednesday's futures expiry, brokers said.

"The bolsa mostly rose on futures expiry tomorrow but CRT also caused a rise," said one dealer, referring to sale of a 35-percent stake in Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT). The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares ended up 1.95 percent at 67,846 points on hefty volume of 576.1 million reais ($554 million).

He said the rise was due to investors busy buying and selling futures and market reaction to the sale of CRT shares to a group including Brazil's RBS Participacoes and Telefonica de Espana for 681 million reais or 54.8 percent over base price. "It showed Telebras and any other companies linked to telecommunications have very bright prospects," one dealer said.
Telebras, which regularly makes up 65 percent of daily bolsa trade, rose 2.56 percent to close at 78.20 reais while its voting common jumped 3.77 percent to 71.50 reais.
But other telecom issues rose more, led by Telesp preferred, which surged 6.94 reais to close at 207.99 reais.
Prices of most leading shares also increased, including state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce, up 0.05 percent to 19.90 reais, and state power holding Eletrobras, up 0.55 percent to 363 reais.
Some banking shares posted gains, with Banco Itau closing sharply higher at 404 reais, and Banespa ending up a strong 12.36 percent on weak volume at 5.00 reais.
Despite the wider bolsa's rise, the Electrical Energy Index closed up only a modest 0.36 percent at 1,828 points, mostly the result of Eletrobras' rise and a 2.35 percent hike in CPFL preferred.
